_comment: POLICY RECORD, not live config (#245). Claude Code loads hooks from
settings files with NO content verification, NO cross-session approval,
and live file-watching — so a checked-out branch that modified either
the hook scripts or a committed hooks block would execute silently.
The live wiring therefore resides in .claude/settings.local.json
(untracked, symlink-shared across worktrees), installed from this
template ONLY by a maintainer running ./scripts/pin-hooks.sh after
reviewing the diff. Every command verifies ALL hook scripts against
the local TOFU pin store (.claude/hooks.sha256, also untracked)
before executing — mismatch fails closed with a re-pin instruction.
Each command also REFUSES a pin store that is tracked in git: git
silently overwrites gitignored files on checkout, so a force-tracked
(git add -f) pin file would otherwise substitute the trust anchor —
the security-review P1 on PR #269. ci.yml carries the matching gate.
Commands first no-op when .claude/hooks-wiring.json is absent, so the
same wiring is safe to deploy machine-globally via managed settings
(allowManagedHooksOnly) — the COMPLETE fix for the checkout-time
Never re-add a hooks block to the committed .claude/settings.json.

hooks.command: sh -c 'if [ ! -f .claude/hooks-wiring.json ]; then exit 0; fi; if git ls-files --error-unmatch .claude/hooks.sha256 >/dev/null 2>&1; then echo "BLOCKED: .claude/hooks.sha256 is TRACKED in git — the checked-out branch is supplying its own hook pins (#245). Remove it from the branch, restore your pins: ./scripts/pin-hooks.sh" >&2; exit 2; fi; if command -v shasum >/dev/null 2>&1; then shasum -a 256 -c .claude/hooks.sha256 >/dev/null 2>&1; else sha256sum -c .claude/hooks.sha256 >/dev/null 2>&1; fi || { echo "BLOCKED: .claude/hooks/* does not match the local TOFU pins (.claude/hooks.sha256). If you just checked out or pulled a branch, REVIEW the hook diffs, then re-pin: ./scripts/pin-hooks.sh (#245)" >&2; exit 2; }; exec .claude/hooks/format-python.sh'
